drivers.text: Revenue grew 26% on higher advertising revenue: ad impressions up 10% and average price per ad up 14% year over year.

Operating income fell 37% because costs rose: the $9.89 billion attorneys general charge, data center and technical infrastructure expense (including third-party cloud), and third-party AI token costs.
Excluding the legal charge, management says Q3 operating income would have been $22.88 billion, up from $20.535 billion; headcount is down 15% year over year.
Management expects to keep investing aggressively in 2027 for core business and AI; current and scheduled capacity gives flexibility across model training, core growth and new products.
Capex outlook was narrowed to $135-145 billion for 2026 (prior $130-145 billion), and Reality Labs losses are expected at $18-19 billion.

gaps: cloud_segment_*: Meta has no cloud segment (segments are Family of Apps and Reality Labs); cloud revenue and cloud operating income are not applicable.
rpo_total, rpo_next_12m_pct: not disclosed for Meta in these files (no remaining performance obligations of note found).

The filings do not use the name 'Hyperion'; the 10-Q describes two unconsolidated data center ventures called the Louisiana Venture (Oct 2025) and Texas Venture (Jul 2026), each 20% owned, with estimated development costs of 27 and 14 billion (numbers on lines 502 and 504, split across lines). Whether the Louisiana Venture is the one the article calls Hyperion is not stated in the files.
